FARIDABAD: "I don't talk to pups; send your father." That was allegedly what Monu Sharma told Shaurya, son of senior IT executive Paramjeet Dhankar, during a confrontation over a damaged gate in their common parking area, news agency PTI reported.
The exchange, which took place on Friday, set off a chain of events that led Dhankar to approach a police post to complain against his neighbour. But what followed there was even more disturbing: When police summoned Sharma, he allegedly threatened to kill Dhankar before the night was over.
Hours later, the threat allegedly turned into reality. Sharma called Dhankar downstairs from his house in Faridabad's Sector 21C on the pretext of discussing a car parking issue and opened fire at him with a licensed pistol.
Fifteen rounds were fired, nine of which are believed to have hit the 45-year-old executive, killing him on the spot. His son, who was also targeted, survived by taking cover behind parked vehicles.
‘I will not leave you alive by tonight’
According to police sources, the confrontation began after Shaurya approached Sharma over a damaged gate in the common parking area and sought repairs. Sharma allegedly refused to speak to him, telling him to send his father instead, news agency PTI reported.
Dhankar, who lived in Singapore, had returned to India on Thursday to celebrate Diwali and attend his nephew's wedding. After learning about the exchange, he went to Ankhir police chowki and lodged a complaint against Sharma, sources said.
Police subsequently called Sharma to the post to address the complaint. It was here that Sharma allegedly issued an explicit death threat to Dhankar in front of police personnel.
"I will not leave you alive by tonight," he allegedly told Dhankar, according to police sources.
Despite the threat, officials reportedly helped the two sides reach a compromise, allegedly considering Sharma's warning hollow. The victim's friends later questioned why police did not take the threat seriously or act against Sharma.
From police post to parking lot: What happened next
Around 8.30pm on Friday, Sharma allegedly rang the bell at Dhankar's ground-floor residence in house No. 641 and called him downstairs, asking him to move his car.
Shaurya accompanied his father to the parking area. An argument reportedly broke out, following which Sharma allegedly pulled out his licensed pistol and fired at close range.
According to police, 15 rounds were fired. Nine bullets are believed to have struck Dhankar, though the exact number will be confirmed after the postmortem. Sharma allegedly also fired at Shaurya, who escaped by taking cover behind parked vehicles.
Dhankar tried to flee but collapsed and died at the spot before he could be taken to hospital. The accused fled in his car with his family.
Police teams from Surajkund police station, the crime branch and the forensic science laboratory reached the spot and collected evidence, including empty cartridges. Bullet marks were visible on parking pillars and vehicles, while bloodstains marked the road where Dhankar fell.
A history of quarrels between neighbours
The confrontation at the police post was the latest in a series of disputes between the two families, who lived in the same building. Sharma occupied the second floor with his wife, son and daughter, while Dhankar and his family lived on the ground floor.
Around five days before the murder, Sharma had allegedly abused Shaurya during an argument over his pet dog defecating in the common parking area. Dhankar's family lodged a police complaint, but the matter was later settled.
Dhankar's father, Mange Ram, also alleged that Sharma had damaged their house gate, prompting another police complaint two to three days before the shooting. He further accused Sharma of recently assaulting an 85-year-old neighbour in the building.
"Mohan is a notorious man, and he recently assaulted another 85-year-old neighbour in the building. He had also damaged our house gate three days back, following which we lodged a police complaint as well. On Friday, he called my son downstairs on the pretext of asking him to move his car and fired at him, killing him on the spot. There is ample space in the parking area. My son was a very decent man," Mange Ram said.
Accused arrested in Ballabhgarh
A crime branch team arrested Sharma near DLF Chowk in Ballabhgarh on Saturday. Police said he would be produced before a court and taken on remand for questioning and collection of evidence.
"Based on the complaint of Paramjeet's son Shaurya, a case has been registered against Monu Sharma alias Mohan, his wife Divya, son Mayank, daughter Naina and brother Hetram. Paramjeet's body has been sent to the civil hospital for a postmortem. We have arrested the main accused, Monu Sharma, and are questioning him," Surajkund SHO Prahlad Singh said.
A case was registered at Surajkund police station under sections 103 (murder), 109 (attempt to murder) and 61(2) (criminal conspiracy) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.
Dhankar was senior vice-president at Singapore-based FPT Software Company Ltd and had earlier headed Tech Mahindra's Asia-Pacific regional business operations. Originally from Hisar, he had returned from Singapore on November 5 for his nephew's wedding, scheduled for November 24. He is survived by his wife, son, daughter and parents.

Ayodhya lit up with thousands of earthen lamps on Saturday as the city celebrated the 10th edition of Deepotsav, with more than 30 lakh diyas set to illuminate 56 ghats along the banks of the Saryu River.
The grand celebration showcased the city's rich spiritual and cultural heritage, with the illuminated ghats presenting a spectacular display of devotion and tradition, adding to the spiritual splendour of Shri Ayodhya Dham.

Vice President CP Radhakrishnan, Uttar Pradesh Governor Anandiben Patel and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath attended the celebrations, along with saints and other prominent guests.

Finland is looking to Ukraine’s defence experience as the country seeks to fortify a 1,340 kilometre border with Russia.
Finland’s army commander, Lieutenant General Pasi Välimäki, said Kyiv’s “extensive defense lines” and anti-tank obstacles has helped to slow down Russia’s attacks.

“If we build fortifications and dig anti-tank ditches or obstacles as deep as those in Ukraine, how long does it take before our environment turns them into artificial ponds?”
The lieutenant also stressed that Russia has already started to rebuild its military and weapons stockpile, with the likes of T-90 tanks, BMP-3 infantry fighting vehicles delivered to storage facilities.
While Finland is unable to prevent Moscow from rearming, Välimäki said they are aiming to create “barrier” so that Russia cannot move any further towards Finland, or an alliance.
It comes as both Finland and Norway broke convention to speak directly to Vladimir Putin last week, sparking fury from European leaders.

But the move attracted criticism from their Nordic counterparts including Danish prime minister Mette Frederiksen as they urged Europe’s leaders to “stick together” on Ukraine.
In a joint statement, Stoere said he and Stubb had spoken to Putin for about 90 minutes, and linked the initiative to planned peace discussions between Russian, Ukrainian and US officials in Abu Dhabi next month. The discussions will be their first since February.
They said they had then spoken to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky as Ukrainian foreign minister Andrii Sybiha confirmed the call had been coordinated with Kyiv, calling it "the right approach".
"We welcome such active support for our diplomatic efforts and peace process," he said, adding that he also hoped a local ceasefire around the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky could "pave the way to other steps in the peace process."
"The discussion was frank and substantive,” Stubb said. “We are neighbouring countries to Russia. The outcome of this war will have a direct impact on our and the broader European security. Ending the war requires direct discussions.”
Stoere said he and Stubb had "stressed the importance of de-escalation,” and that both had voiced strong support for Ukraine.

Many people are not big fans of game publisher EA right now for good reason, but for those who remember a better time in the 1990s, there’s a little good news. Twenty-five classic games from that EA era have been lightly remastered and updated, then placed for sale on Steam and GOG, including several Wing Commander games and nearly the entire Ultima series.
Below is the full list of remastered or re-released games:
- Road Rash: 30th Anniversary Edition
- Wing Commander: 35th Anniversary Edition
- Wing Commander II: Vengeance of the Kilrathi: 35th Anniversary Edition
- Wing Commander III: Heart of the Tiger: 30th Anniversary Edition
- Wing Commander IV: The Price of Freedom: 30th Anniversary Edition
- Wing Commander Prophecy: 30th Anniversary Edition
- Privateer 2: The Darkening: 30th Anniversary Edition
- Wing Commander: Privateer
- Wing Commander: Academy
- Wing Commander: Armada
- Strike Commander

- Ultima VI: The False Prophet
- Ultima VII: The Complete Edition
- Ultima VIII: Gold Edition
- Ultima IX: Ascension
- Ultima Underworld I
- Ultima Underworld II
The story behind seven remasters
In a lengthy blog post published this week, Jim Vessella, a senior producer at EA, described the efforts that went into remastering Wing Commander I-IV and Prophecy, Privateer 2, and Road Rash.
It’s a long, detailed story that’s worth reading yourself, but here’s a top-level summary. After working on the mostly widely acclaimed Command & Conquer: Remastered Collection in 2019, Vessella writes that he learned about and visited a room at EA’s Redwood Shores campus that contained a large archive of poorly labeled or sorted physical media from ages past.
In his free time, and with the help of others, he began cataloging this archive and discovered, among other things, that it contained virtually the entirety of the original masters of Wing Commander III and Wing Commander IV‘s full-motion-video cutscenes.
The story that ensues involves building a small team of contractors, poring through the footage 17 hours a day on swing shifts to label and digitize it, and then coordinating with several key community members—particularly Matt Wells, who has made community enhancement patches for some of the Wing Commander games—to put together remasters of those games.

Syncing Apple Music across your devices is easier than you think
Using Apple Music on multiple devices? Keeping them in sync is a breeze.
Apple Music is one of the best music streaming platforms right now, especially for Apple device owners. But despite its association with the tech giant, Apple Music is not exclusive to Apple devices and is available on multiple platforms. You can, for example, sign in with your Apple Account and listen to your favorite songs on an Android phone, Windows PC or even smart TVs.
After signing in on a new device, though, you may notice that your music library isn't synced and your songs aren't there. If this has happened to you, don't worry. Changing a single setting in Apple Music will prompt it to sync your music across all your devices, ensuring you don't have to manage your library manually on each one.
How to turn on Sync Library on Apple Music
The main reason Apple Music might not sync your library across devices is that you're using different accounts on each device, so check that first. If you're not sure which account you're using, open the Apple Music app and tap your profile picture on the Home tab. If the email address on the unsynced device doesn't match, you're signed in on a different account. Sign out, then log in using your primary Apple Account.
Now make sure Sync Library is enabled on your devices. On your iPhone or iPad, open Settings and look for Apps. Then, find the Music app in the list and enable Sync Library. On a Mac, open the Music app and click the "Music" menu at the top of the screen, then go to Settings. Now, under the General tab, make sure Sync Library is enabled and click OK to save your settings. The process is pretty much the same in Windows, but you need to click the three-dot button instead to find Settings. If you have an Android phone, this option is enabled by default, and you don't need to change anything.
No matter the platform, the first sync might take a while, especially if you have a large music library. If you don't see your songs right away after enabling syncing, leave the Music app open and wait a few minutes.
What to do when Apple Music won't sync
In the Mac app, click the File menu, then go to Library and select Update Cloud Library — this will force the app to sync and check for updates in your personal library. This option is also available in the Windows app and can be found in the sidebar. Unfortunately, the Android and iOS apps don't have that option.
Also, make sure your mobile devices are connected to Wi-Fi and not in Low Power Mode, as this may prevent them from syncing your music library. If nothing else has worked, your best option is to go back to Settings, turn off Sync Library and then turn it back on. You can also try signing out of your Apple Account and logging back in. If you don't subscribe to Apple Music and have an offline library on your Mac or PC, the only way to sync your library is to manually transfer the Music folder to another computer via Apple iTunes or Apple Devices.
Syncing behavior isn't the only setting you might want to change in Apple Music. While you're there, it's worth exploring some other toggles, like changing the audio quality options to enable lossless audio.

With rolling heat waves sweeping the globe, 2027 is shaping up to be the hottest year on record. As the health risks of extreme temperatures mount, there's never been a better time to rethink sustainable cooling.
Air conditioners and electric fans account for around 20 percent of electricity used in buildings worldwide—3 to 4 percent of total greenhouse gas emissions—and, as demand for cooling in homes, workplaces, and schools grows, the number of AC units in use could reach 5.5 billion by 2050.
The solution isn't one magic fix, but a suite of emerging technologies heading for living rooms and apartment windows. From radar sensors tracking your body to compact heat pumps and climate-safe refrigerants, here is how the next generation of air-conditioning plans to keep us cool without cooking the planet.
The “Intelligent AC” Boom
In 1994, Mitsubishi Electric was zooming past the air-con competition, introducing the first motion and occupancy sensors for AC, with infrared 3D sensing eventually following in the mid-2010s. Fast-forward to 2026 and AI-powered ACs now track people in the home with millimeter-level precision.
AC makers have launched intelligent, targeted air conditioner units all year, from Samsung’s Bespoke AI system in March to Dyson’s Find+Follow feature for its Purifier Cool fan in June. At IFA in September, we got a whole sweep from Chinese companies like Hisense, Dreo, and Midea.
LG’s latest DualCool AI AC has a 5-meter radar sensor for people detection plus targeting based on your everyday movement patterns. Hisense’s Companion Living AC also uses data from smart home sensors to identify and precool “target paths” within the home, based on your routines. So if you always head from the couch to the kitchen for a midnight snack, your AC can cool that particular zone before you even get up.
The real-time cooling features aim to improve comfort inside sticky homes. A secondary benefit is that precisely locating people and delivering cooling directly to them could reduce energy consumption. “It definitely has the potential to reduce the total energy use for air-conditioning,” says Björn Palm, senior professor in energy technology at the KTH Royal Institute of Technology in Stockholm. By how much? That's less clear.
Dyson’s Find+Follow purifier and fan uses a simple, low-resolution camera, feeding the “stick figure”-like, anonymous coordinates of its 17-point person detection into an algorithm, all instantly processed on-device and deleted, without any face recognition. “It can tell that you’re a human, whether you’re sitting or standing, which direction you’re moving," says Alex Hudson, an environmental care engineer at Dyson. "It might map your arms and shoulders.”
The Purifier Cool can oscillate 350 degrees between “up to six people” in the space, directing airflow for personalized cooling. One hour after it detects that everyone has left the room, the appliance will switch to Auto mode and—if there is no big pollution spike for the purifier to deal with, like a truck driving past an open window—it’s a "considerably lower power draw than when it’s in fan mode, so there’s definitely a benefit there,” Hudson says.
Samsung’s Bespoke AI WindFree Pro adds a motion radar sensor, which can recognize and track two occupants. “AI Direct Wind” can follow and blast you for immediate cooling, whereas “AI Indirect Wind,” you guessed it, cools the spot you’re in without blowing air right in your face. Samsung’s residential environment tests claim energy savings of “up to 30 percent” with its overall AI energy mode switched on. At IFA, Samsung added wearable data: a Galaxy Watch or Galaxy Ring can signal to the AC when you’ve fallen asleep, triggering a gentler Windfree Cooling mode overnight.
Midea’s VitaBreeze AC, launching in early 2027, combines user photos with millimeter-wave radar sensors to personalize cooling. During setup, the user manually uploads a series of room images to the app, indicating the air conditioner placement. The AC then uses those images with radar data to create a 3D virtual grid of the room and furniture position.
Millimeter wave (or mmWave) radar—the kind used in 5G cellular technology—bounces short-wavelength radio waves, typically 1 to 10 millimeters, to detect an object's distance and angle, as well as tiny movements in real time. Here, the Midea app’s Follow Me feature, similar to Samsung's, can pinpoint your real-time position in the room, triggering louver adjustments as you move around. Manuel Seethaler, head of Midea's Residential Air Conditioning product strategy in Europe, says that its technology can save more than 30 percent of energy in cooling mode compared with units without these algorithms.
The average AC sold in 2024 was already about 20 percent more efficient than an equivalent model in 2014. However, there’s still plenty of room to grow, as the IEA predicts that “cooling demand” will grow by 1,600 terawatt-hours by 2035—Japan and South Korea’s total electricity combined. But this kind of proximity sensing could also result in marginal energy savings.
“There is a performance improvement you can get if [targeted AC] is done well,” says Vincent Romanin, founder and CTO of San Francisco–based Gradient, which makes 120-volt all-weather window AC/heat pumps. “But we’re going into buildings where we’re reducing the energy by 85 percent and to design another feature that gets us to 87 percent? I personally have never used a product with an occupancy sensor that I feel like worked well.”
Compact Window ACs
For Palm, to reach sustainable home cooling by 2050, we need three major changes: cheaper, compact heat pumps for all home sizes; fewer toxic natural refrigerants (fluids and chemical compounds that absorb and release heat); and newly designed systems with low charge to ensure safety.
Heat pumps have become a modern, efficient option for heating and cooling. For heating, it's a four-stage process: absorbing outside heat to produce gas via a refrigerant; compressing to raise the temperature; condensing, where heat is passed to the water in your home’s heating system; and cooling back into a liquid via an expansion valve to drop the pressure. When cooling is needed, the reversing valve switches back to run the process from inside to outside for air-conditioning.
The key is to persuade renters and people living in smaller homes to make the overall switch. “For the domestic market, we need heat pumps which fit into an apartment without being too noisy or bulky,” Palm says. It's also critical to reduce the price.
Gradient units typically use one-third less energy than a standard window AC, mostly for heating but with cooling efficiencies too. They’re a quick self-install option that lets apartment renters get their window back, see lower bills, and run a quieter AC system than older models.
But fixing the form factor only solves part of the equation. Palm’s other criteria—replacing toxic synthetic refrigerants with natural alternatives like propane (R290), as in Bosch's Climate 6000iP, which launched in September—present a tougher engineering challenge. Leaking refrigerants alone account for an estimated 720 million metric tons of CO2-equivalent emissions every year. Natural refrigerants dramatically curb the potential for global warming, but their flammability demands complex, spark-free redesigns and low-charge systems that US regulators and supply chains are still cautious about embracing.
Reaching sustainable cooling by 2050 won’t be glamorous, Palm says. Ultimately, the future of home cooling won't hinge on an air conditioner that tracks you to the kitchen for a midnight snack—it depends on the unsexy, invisible mechanical work happening deep inside the compressor.

Quick Answer
You can run AI models locally on Android and iPhone using Google AI Edge Gallery or PocketPal AI, and on Mac and Windows using LM Studio or Ollama. Simply install the app, download a compatible AI model, and start using it offline. Your data stays on your device, with no cloud access required after setup.
While many think AI is a bubble that is going to burst one day, it might be true, or it might not be at all. Only time will tell. But we should all accept that AI is fundamentally changing how we interact with our devices and do work.
For me, my life revolves around AI: I hand off some of my work to it and do things that once weren’t possible.
AI models are rapidly evolving. If you don’t know what an AI model is, it powers the apps and interfaces you interact with. For instance, the ChatGPT app uses GPT models, and the Claude app is powered by Claude models, which run behind the scenes.
While AI is fundamentally changing how we interact with devices and making work easier, handing your sensitive data to it has remained a major privacy concern.But thanks to rapid AI model development, many capable, powerful AI models enough to run locally on your device, without your data leaving your device
Companies like Google and Meta offer free AI models that can run locally on most consumer devices, including your mobile phone. Apps like Google’s AI Edge Gallery and PocketPal AI also make it easy to discover and run AI models locally without technical expertise.
If you have a capable computer with decent RAM, you can also run AI models locally to use them for writing your email, summarising PDFs, data analysis, coding, using their vision capabilities, and much more.
However, setting up an AI model locally involves downloading the app, choosing the model yourself, and understanding its capabilities first.
To help you out, I have created this detailed, comprehensive guide to set up and run local AI models on your device on Android, iPhone, Mac, or even on Windows.
I wrote this guide with beginners in mind, so every step is comprehensive and easy to follow. If you have questions, comment below. I am happy to help you. Most of these models can run locally on many consumer applications, but before that, don’t forget to check our prerequisites because that’s where your journey starts.
Table of Contents
Pre-Requirements To Run AI Models Locally on Device
Your device’s RAM determines whether it can run AI models.
Technically, a model loads into your RAM to run. As a general rule of thumb, a model needs about as much free RAM as its download size.
So, more RAM leaves room to run large AI models. A minimum of 6 GB of RAM is required to run decent, capable AI models locally on your device
Similarly, you need enough storage to download and store models locally. A model can generally range from 2 GB to 20 GB or even more, depending on its size and capabilities.
Finally, you need an internet connection and enough data to download the model so you can run it offline.
As I said before, these models can range from 2 GB to 20 GB. So it requires an internet connection to download the model and store it locally on your device.
Of course, Other minimum specifications, such as a capable Processor, Operating system, and platform, also matter but not as much as RAM does.
How to check how much RAM your device has
On Android:
Go to About Device to see how much RAM your smartphone has. To do that: Open Settings on your device, tap on the search bar at the top, and search for “About Device”. On some phones, scroll down and tap “About Device”. Look at the RAM specifications.
On some phones, you will see extra visible RAM after the plus sign, for example, 16GB + 12GB. However, only the first number is the real memory.
iPhone:
Apple generally doesn’t disclose the RAM used in iPhones. However, iPhone 15 Pro and newer devices generally have at least 8GB, while older iPhones have less than 6GB, which can run 1 billion to 2 billion models. You can check how much RAM your iPhone has from here.
Mac:
To check how much RAM on your MacBook: From the home screen, click on the Apple icon in the top left corner screen and tap on About This Mac. From here, you can check chip and memory options. Apple MacBooks running on Apple Silicon are especially good for running local AI models since the graphics chip shares all the memory.
Windows:
On Windows, you can go to Settings > System > About. From there, check the installed RAM, graphics card, and system type (x86 or ARM-based), which determines which applications you can download to run AI models locally.
Once your device meets the minimum RAM requirement, follow these steps to set it up to run AI models locally. Use the table of contents above to go to the device you want to set up. This guide covers Android, iPhone, Mac, and Windows.
How to Run AI Models Locally on Any Device
Android:
Method 1: Run Gemma 4 on Android with Google AI Edge Gallery
You can run Google’s family of Open-weight AI models locally for free on your Android device using Google’s own AI Edge Gallery app (Free).
Gemma 4 is Google’s latest open-weight model. It comes in five model sizes. Gemma 4 E2B and Gemma 4 E4B are suitable for running on Android devices. 2B requires at least 8GB of RAM, and 4B requires at least 12GB of RAM.
Gemma 4 also supports vision capabilities, so it is not just text; you can also use it to understand images.
How to install and run the latest Google Gemma 4 models locally on your Android phone
Step 1: Download Google AI Edge Gallery from the Play Store. Here is the direct download link.
Step 2: Open the app and tap on AI Chat.
Step 3: Under the recommended models, tap Download below. To download the model you want. Gemma 4 E2B is 2.6 GB and best for starters, while Gemma 4 E4B is 3.7 GB and smarter, but your phone needs at least 8 GB of RAM to run it locally.
Step 3: Once the model is downloaded, tap Try it.
Step 4: Type your prompt in the Type prompt box and tap the send button.
Step 5: Like the other AI apps, the model replies to your prompt. You can also see how fast the model runs, measured in tokens per second, and how much RAM it uses. On my Android phone, the Gemma 4 E2B model ran at about 30 tokens per second, and my model comes with 16 GB of RAM.
Method 2: Run any open model on Android with PocketPal AI
PocketPal is a popular free and open-source app for running AI models locally on Android.
Unlike Google’s AI Edge Gallery, it supports a wide variety of third-party models, including Google’s Gemma, Meta’s Llama, Microsoft’s Phi, Qwen, and more. It also supports GGUF models, including compressed versions.
How do I use the PocketPal app to run AI models locally on my device?
Step 1: Download and install the PocketPal app from the Google Play Store. Here is the direct download link.
Step 2: Open the app and, during onboarding, tap Download Model.
Step 3: Pick any available model to download and tap Download,
or tap the plus option to find more. To get a new model, tap the plus icon, select Hugging Face, then tap Choose and add from Hugging Face.
Step 4: From here, you can search for any model. In this case, I searched for the Qwen3 1.7B parameter model and tapped the download icon to download it locally.
Step 5: Once done, open the Models tab and select the model to load it. Now go to the chat interface and enter the prompt, and the model uses the model that you have loaded, in this case, the Qwen3 1.7 billion parameter model, to answer your queries. You can also see how much time it takes to run this model on your device.
iPhone
Method 1: Run Gemma 4 on iPhone with Google AI Edge Gallery
Google’s AI Edge Gallery is also available on iPhone and supports the latest Gemma 4 family of open-weight models, similar to Android. You can download and use E2B (around 2.6 GB) and the E4B model (around 3.7 GB).
Apple doesn’t disclose the RAM used on iPhones. However, the latest iPhone models, including the iPhone 15 Pro and later, support up to 8 GB of RAM, which can run these models faster and more reliably. However, older iPhones may struggle with slow responses, battery drain, and overheating, so keep that in mind.
Step 1: Download the Google AI Edge Gallery app on your iPhone. Here is the link.
Step 2: Open the app and tap on AI chat
Step 3: Now download the compatible AI model. In this case, I’m downloading Gemma 4 E2B, which is about 2.59 GB. Click on the download icon under the model.
Step 4: Wait for the model to download, then tap Try It, enter the prompt, and wait for a reply. If you want to use the vision capabilities, tap on the plus icon and upload an image
Method 2: Run open models on iPhone with PocketPal AI
Similar to Google’s AI Edge Gallery app, the PocketPal app is also available on iPhone. It also gives access to some of the popular Hugging Face model library and other third-party models, including models from Meta, Cohere, and more. It also supports Google Gemma 4 models.
Step 1: Install the PocketPal AI app on your iPhone. Here is the link.
Step 2: Open the app, tap Download Model, select a model, and tap Download. In this case, I am downloading the Qwen3 1.7B model.
Step 3: Once downloaded, tap the Load option at the top, enter the prompt, and wait for the reply
Mac
Method 1: Run AI models on a Mac with LM Studio
You can use LM Studio on Mac to run AI models locally.
It supports a wide range of models, including models from Google Gemma, Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral, and more. Like the mobile app, you can install LM Studio on your Mac, download a model, and start chatting. It also supports GGUF and Apple-optimized MLX models.
Depending on the model, you can have text conversations, image analysis, and more. You can also use it as a local API for other apps.
However, LM Studio is only available on Apple Silicon Macs (M1 or later). Intel Macs are not supported.
How to install and run AI models locally using LM Studio on Mac
Step 1: First, go to lmstudio.ai/download and download the LM Studio app for Mac. Select the compatible version and drag and drop LM Studio into Applications to install it.
Step 2: Open LM Studio on the Mac, click on the model search in the sidebar, and search for the model; for example, in this case, I searched for the Gemma 4 E4B model
Step 3: You can also pick a different model, select it, and click Download. A likely fit badge here means that it is suitable to run locally on your Mac using your Mac’s available memory. Once the model is downloaded, tap on Use in the new chat instead.
Step 4: On the home screen, click Load Model in the dialog and select the model. You can also raise the context length here if you are planning for long conversations.
Step 5: Now enter the prompt and press Enter. The model returns with an option. You can also click the model server in the sidebar and turn on the status to use the model for other apps via an OpenAI-compatible API at http://localhost:1234.
Method 2: Run AI models on a Mac with Ollama
You can also run AI models on your Mac using Ollama. It is a free, lightweight tool by Meta that lets you run local AI models in the terminal with one command. It also works with many local apps that support local AI.
Step 1: To run Ollama locally on your device, go to ollama.com/download and click on the Download manually option. You can also directly paste the command into the terminal if you are a developer.
Step 2: Next, open the Ollama.dmg, drag it into Applications, and open it
Step 3: On the onboarding screen, while setting up an account, Ollama asks you to sign up for an account; however, you can tap on No thanks, I will use Ollama locally’
Step 4: Next, to run ollama run llama3, copy the ollama run llama3 command, open Terminal, and paste it. Wait for the model to download completely. Ollama can run Qwen3 4B parameters and other models. In this case, I am going to run the Ollama run Qwen3 4B model. So, wait for the model to download completely.
Step 5: Finally, you can start using the Ollama model right there. You can enter the prompt directly, and it will reply in the same terminal.
Windows
Method 1: Run AI models on Windows with LM Studio
You can use the same LM Studio on Windows as well to run AI models locally on your device
Step 1: Download and install LM Studio for Windows. Here is the download page link.
Step 2: Open the LM Studio app and, in the left sidebar, tap Model Search and search for the model you want to run locally. In this case, Iam using Qwen3 1.7 billion parameters; on the model details page, click the download option.
Step 3: Wait for it to download, and once it has downloaded, tap on Use in new chat
Step 4: Now, on the home screen, in the model box, select the downloaded model. You can tap on the model to select and enable it, then enter the prompt and press enter.
Method 2: Run AI models on Windows with Ollama
Ollama is also available on Mac. It supports NVIDIA and AMD graphics cards, as well as the latest ARM-based Snapdragon PCs. You can download models and use them directly from the terminal. Here is how.
Step 1: First, download Ollama on Windows. Go to ollama.com/download/windows and click Manual download. If you are a developer, you can install it directly in PowerShell using the PowerShell command.
Step 2: Now install the Ollama app on Windows. While setting up, click Continue, and then tap on No thanks, I will use Ollama locally, so you can skip creating an account.
Step 3: Next, copy the command shown in the app, open Terminal, and run this command: ollama run qwen3:1.7b, and press Enter. It downloads the model. Wait for the download to complete.
Step 4: Now enter your question and press Enter.
This is how you can set up and run AI models locally on Android, iPhone, Windows, and Mac. Choosing the right model is important to get high-quality output. Bigger models don’t always mean better outputs, as their capabilities can vary. Our guide to the best AI models to run locally should help you choose the right model for your needs. What we know so far after Krakow gun attack
- Published
At least six people were killed and several others injured when a gunman suspected to have ties to the far-right opened fire in central Krakow, the second largest city in Poland.
Three bodies were found at his home when it was searched by police. Here's everything we know so far.
How did the attack unfold?
The attack began shortly before 15:00 local time (14:00 GMT) in Krakow's Main Market Square, the bustling central point of the city.
Police said a man drove into the square before beginning to fire "at random people from his car".
Footage from the scene shows scenes of panic as people fled, with the sound of gunfire clearly heard.
A passing tram was shot at during the apparently random attack, shattering windows but no passengers were injured.
Armed officers raced to the scene and engaged in a gunfight with the attacker, who was shot within three minutes of the attack beginning, preventing a further massacre, officials said.
The gunman was shot but is alive and has been arrested.
Distressing footage authenticated by BBC Verify shows the moment a police officer confronts the suspect on the ground before firing his weapon several times.
The officer then falls to the ground, apparently having been injured himself.
Shop windows in the square have signs of damage, seemingly from bullets, with glass shards scattered along the floor.
City officials have urged people who live in the city and tourists to stay away from the area while an investigation continues.
The suspect's car, found at the intersection of Dietla and Stradomska streets, is being checked for possible explosive devices, police say. Residents of nearby buildings are being evacuated while the operation is under way.
How many people have died and been injured?
Six people - four women and two men - are confirmed to have been killed, including a British national. Three victims are Polish and two have not been identified.
Sixteen people, including five foreigners and the attacker, were taken to hospital. Among those being treated are two police officers who were shot while detaining the attacker.
Poland's Prime Minister Donald Tusk later named the injured officers as Senior Constable Jakub Kulik and Senior Constable Artur Morański.
Tusk said three bodies - two women and one man - were found at the gunman's house when it was searched after the attack.
One of the police officers was described as being in a "very critical condition" by a Polish government minister after being shot three times while arresting the attacker. The officer is undergoing surgery, he added.
Polish authorities have not confirmed the names and ages of the other victims.
What do we know about the suspect and motive?
Police have identified the attacker as a 25-year-old Polish man but have not confirmed his name.
The suspect was wearing "military-style attire" and had a military-grade weapon, according to a police spokesperson. However, authorities have confirmed the attacker was not a soldier.
"Many pieces of weapons and ammunition were found in his vehicle", the spokesperson added.
Polish media has reported the suspect had a firearms permit and may have obtained the weapons from his family home.
A minister has said early investigations indicate he was inspired by "far-right ideologies". The minister also described him as an "ultra-nationalist" without giving further details.
His home is being searched with support from counter-terrorism police.
How did witnesses describe the attack?
The shooting happened in one of the largest medieval squares in Europe, a busy location which is also a popular tourist destination.
Jonathan Balshaw from Ipswich was there with his Polish girlfriend Dominika. The couple were outside St Mary's Basilica, in the corner of the square, when the shooting started.
Jonathan said: "We ran down the side of the church and through the side door and hid with several other people until the gunfire died down.
"A lot of shots were fired, more than 20 with it sounding like multiple different firearms - there were two distinctly different noises."
Caitlin Shasby from Newcastle arrived in Krakow yesterday with her friend Jon for a long weekend.
She said they heard shots from their hotel room but were not sure what was happening until their hotel rang them and told them to "stay in our rooms until further notice".
What has the reaction been in Poland and internationally?
After travelling to Krakow, Prime Minister Donald Tusk said : "Until now in Poland we haven't had such drastic cases of terrorism...that's what we have to call this cruel attack on people's lives here in Krakow."
Krakow Mayor Łukasz Gibała has signed an order declaring a period of mourning in the city which will last until Wednesday, 11 November.
US ambassador to Poland Tom Rose described it as a "savage and murderous attack".
The EU's top diplomat, Kaja Kallas, said the shooting was "a tragedy that will be felt far beyond Poland".

With Stephen Miller pick, Trump readies for a battle
- Published
In the aftermath of the Republican Party's sweeping defeat in Tuesday's midterm elections, Donald Trump said he would be willing to work with the newly ascendent Democrats in Congress.
On Friday, however, he elevated Stephen Miller, his bare-knuckled political operative and longtime adviser, to replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff.
Far from an olive branch to Congress, Miller's promotion could be a sign that the president is girding for political battle by installing a partisan firebrand in the top White House job.
"The mission now is more clear than ever: Fight with all of our soul to support our president and defend this magnificent republic," Miller posted on X, adding that he was "honored beyond words" to be Trump's pick for the job.
One of the most powerful positions in Washington, the chief of staff is gatekeeper to the president, agenda-setter in the White House and chief negotiator with Congress and other outside political interests.
"Stephen Miller's been with me since the beginning," Trump said in comments to reporters after announcing the move on his Truth Social website. "He gets it."
Miller is best known for being the driving force behind the Trump administration's aggressive immigration enforcement policies, which has included ramping up funding for enforcement operations across the US.
He made headlines when he called Alex Pretti, who was shot and killed by federal immigration officials during a massive deportation operation in Minneapolis, a "domestic terrorist" and an "assassin". He would later walk back those words, saying federal agents "may not have been following" proper protocol.
He has also reportedly played a leading role in the US military operations in Venezuela and against suspected drug trafficking operations in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific, which critics have condemned as extra-judicial killings.
Miller joined Trump's political operation early in his 2016 presidential bid as a strategist and incendiary warm-up speaker at his raucous campaign rallies.
He was one of the few senior White House staffers to persevere through the entirety of his first term. He stayed loyal to Trump during his political exile following attempts to overturn his ballot-box defeat in 2020 failed. He then returned in the influential role of deputy chief of staff for policy in Trump's second term.
Wiles, who co-managed the president's successful 2024 re-election campaign, developed a reputation as a cool professional who avoided the White House staffing upheavals, dramatic policy reversals and personality clashes that typified Trump's first presidential term.
The president, however, began souring on Wiles in recent months, as his political standing in the US declined, culminating in Tuesday's electoral rout. He also reportedly chafed at news stories indicating that those in Wiles' orbit were landing lucrative consulting jobs through their connections to the president.

Miller's hardline views sets up clash with Congress
While Trump praised Miller's effectiveness as a manager on Friday, working with Congress could prove to be a challenge.
It is difficult to overstate how disliked Miller is by most Democrats – and some Republicans.
"Stephen Miller is a dangerous xenophobe and reckless extremist who has American blood on his hands," Democratic House leader Hakeem Jeffries wrote on X. "His presence in government should be eradicated like a malignant tumor."
Earlier this year, Miller posted on social media that James Talarico, who had just secured the Democratic nomination to run for Senate in Texas, was "their first transgender Senate candidate".
The Democratic Party offered a terse, obscenity laced reply, telling Miller to shut up.
Now Miller will have to negotiate with a US Senate that includes a newly elected Talarico as one of its rising stars, after an election in which polls found that 58% of voters believe the administration's immigration enforcement actions had "gone too far" and Hispanics decisively turned against Republican candidates.
On Wednesday, in a social media post attempting to explain the Republican midterm defeats, Vice-president JD Vance - who is an early frontrunner for the Republican 2028 presidential nomination - wrote that he was "open to the idea that we should change enforcement- by focusing more on businesses that hire illegal labor, for instance".
That now seems less likely with an immigration hardline taking the White House helm.
Thom Tillis, the North Carolina Republican senator who is retiring at the end of the year, has been particularly vocal in condemning Miller. He has called him "incompetent" and "the architect of some of the dumbest proposals from the Trump White House".
Other Republicans, however, have sung his praises.
"Stephen Miller has been a true conservative warrior since his days as a Senate staffer, a staunch defender of law and order against illegal invasions and leftist lawlessness, and a steadfast fighter for President Trump for over a decade," Utah Senator Mike Lee posted on X after Trump's announcement.
At a time when congressional Democrats are promising to launch new investigations and oversight into the Trump administration, it appears that a "warrior" and a "fighter" is the kind of person the president wants to have running his White House.

Diwali celebrations coincide with worsening air. Here’s how to stay safer
For people across South Asia, especially in northern India, Diwali celebrations coincide with the return of hazardous winter air, raising concerns about how to celebrate safely
BENGALURU, India -- For people across South Asia, especially in northern India, Diwali celebrations coincide with the return of hazardous winter air, raising concerns about how to celebrate safely.
Winter also brings severe smog to parts of Pakistan and China, where warmer air can act as a lid, trapping colder air and pollution near the ground. In eastern Europe, burning coal and wood to heat homes also adds to winter pollution. Western Hemisphere countries, meanwhile, face their own seasonal air-quality problems, as summer wildfires send smoke across vast areas of the United States and Canada.
Experts say no matter where you live or when you face pollution, simple steps such as checking the air quality index, wearing a well-fitting mask and using air purifiers can reduce exposure to harmful pollutants.
An estimated 1 billion people worldwide celebrate Diwali, a holiday of Hindus and Jains with ties to ancient epics such as the Ramayana. Fireworks traditionally set off during the holiday, which starts Sunday, can make polluted air more dangerous.
As Diwali approaches, here are ways to reduce exposure to polluted air.
Fireworks add a sharp burst of pollution to a much bigger problem. Across India, Pakistan and other parts of South Asia, traffic, factories, dust from construction and burning of crop residues and waste foul the air. Weak winds and stagnant winter air allow that pollution to build up.
“Poor air quality is our all-year-round problem in our country,” said Shweta Narayan, a public health expert at the Global Climate and Health Alliance. Narayan said firecrackers add to the problem.
India’s air quality index turns pollution measurements into a health warning. AQI readings of 201–300 mean “poor,” 301–400 “very poor” and 401–500 “severe.” Severe levels can harm even healthy people.
Check pollution levels on government or privately run websites before heading outdoors. Look for data from a nearby monitoring station and the time of its last update. A citywide average can conceal a polluted neighborhood.
The problem is especially bad in Delhi, where fine particle pollution averaged about 19 times the World Health Organization’s annual guideline last year. Air pollution monitors have reached the maximum reading they can display multiple times in recent years.
City authorities have responded with temporary construction, industrial and vehicle restrictions. Public health experts said such measures often fail to address the root causes. The city of more than 20 million people is also implementing a long-term plan to promote use of electric vehicles.
Dr. Arvind Kumar, a chest surgeon at Medanta hospital near Delhi and founder trustee of the Lung Care Foundation, recommends using properly fitted N95 or N99 masks outdoors during periods of heavy pollution. These masks are available at pharmacies, hardware stores and online retailers.
N95 filters are designed to capture at least 95% of airborne particles; N99 filters are made to capture at least 99%. The particle respirator masks do not filter harmful gases.
Cover your nose, mouth and chin. Shape the nose clip and check the seal every time. Facial hair can break that seal. The aim, Kumar said, is to ensure “all the breathing is through the mask and not around the mask.”
Replace disposable masks when dirty, damaged or hard to breathe through. Never put a mask on a child younger than 2. People with heart or lung disease should seek medical advice about mask use.
Loose surgical masks, cloth masks and scarves offer unreliable protection against fine particles.
Kumar said pollution can cause persistent coughing, inflame the airways and trigger asthma-like attacks. He also cited increased risks of pneumonia, heart attacks and strokes, while linking prolonged exposure to impaired lung development in children and lung cancer.
Kumar said people should avoid strenuous exercise outdoors during heavy pollution, including early mornings, when pollution levels can be high.
Using the right air purifiers indoors can help. The devices draw in air to filter out pollutants, then recirculate the cleaner air.
A purifier needs enough capacity to clean the air of the room where it runs. Look for a high-efficiency particulate air, or HEPA, filter. Then check its clean air delivery rate, which is the volume of filtered air it supplies.
Place the purifier where you spend the most time, such as the bedroom. Keep its airflow clear and run it consistently.
HEPA filters trap particles. Substantial activated-carbon filters can remove some gases. No purifier removes every pollutant. Avoid machines that deliberately produce ozone, which irritates the lungs.
Cleaner indoor air reduces exposure, but a purifier cannot eliminate pollution’s health risks, Kumar said.
Kumar said it’s important to avoid incense, mosquito coils and candles. Their particles can linger indoors for hours, especially in poorly ventilated rooms, while fireworks pollution can persist overnight, depending on the weather. When many households set off fireworks, their combined emissions can worsen air quality across neighborhoods and entire cities, exposing people who are not taking part. Electric lights can be another way to celebrate Diwali, avoiding toxic gases and smoke from firecrackers.
“If one wants to celebrate and really enjoy the festival of Diwali, avoid bursting firecrackers,” said Narayan, the public health expert.
India’s health ministry also recommends reducing smoky cooking and using a kitchen exhaust that vents outdoors. Damp-mopping floors and wiping dusty surfaces, instead of dry sweeping, can avoid stirring up particles that worsen air quality.
Personal precautions have limits. Narayan said people who earn their livelihoods outdoors cannot simply stay home. Many families also cannot afford air purifiers.
She called for sustained action on pollution sources and affordable health care for those already suffering. Masks and filters can reduce exposure, but lasting protection requires governments to clean the air.
“It’s our responsibility to hold our governments accountable,” Narayan said. “There’s no other way about it.”

The West Bengal Police on November 5 posted a message on X, calling for citizens to celebrate Diwali responsibly. The AI-generated poster showed a stray dog and two cats taking shelter from firecrackers. It said, “Please celebrate responsibly. It’s our Diwali too!”
The post, which was made at 8:29 am, was however taken down within 3 hours. (Archive)
In recent years, campaigns highlighting the environmental impact of firecrackers and calling for restrictions during Diwali have increasingly been framed by a section of the Right wing as an affront to Hindu religious sentiments. The issue of air pollution, consequently, has often been recast as a communal debate, with calls for curbs on firecrackers portrayed as selective targeting of Hindu festivals.
In the same vein, several social media users took offence to Bengal police’s awareness post, claiming that it was a case of selective bias against Hindus. Users began commenting under the post, some of whom went as far as to tag chief minister Suvendu Adhikari, questioning why similar awareness campaigns were allegedly absent during Eid and Christmas.
Some of the comments are displayed in the gallery below. (A few of them contain abusive words. Reader discretion is advised).
Following the backlash, the post was deleted. West Bengal police offered no explanation or clarification as to why the post was removed. Many had anticipated that the West Bengal Police would backtrack on its awareness campaign as this incident forms part of a pattern of state authorities taking down posts on firecracker awareness ahead of Diwali following backlash.
Pattern of Deletion
Alt News had earlier reported that on October 25, Delhi Police had deleted an X post, which raised awareness about a cracker-free Diwali, within hours of posting it. On that occasion, too, social media users had predicted that the post would be removed soon.
Again, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) removed a similar video featuring actress Dia Mirza advocating for a pollution-free Diwali from its social media handles. Both decisions came in the wake of social media outrage from BJP-RSS supporters that these posts hurt the religious sentiments of Hindus. Justice G S Kulkarni of the Bombay high court then directed BMC to re-upload Mirza’s video, remarking “She (Dia Mirza) rendered a really really good message in terms of air pollution… These (opposing Mirza) are stray thoughts of very few people and we should avoid them…”
A video uploaded by AISA president Neha Bora calling for an environment-friendly Diwali was likewise condemned by the Hindutva brigade.
On November 4, actress Soni Razdan’s social media advocacy for a pollution-free Diwali was also derided by several users. “People can’t understand a simple message because they think every statement is about religion,” she retorted to an X post that had targeted her.
Then you are simply unable to see the woods for the trees. It’s not bursting crackers that is anti-national. What is anti national is the fact that you are contributing to the terrible air pollution. My goodness. No wonder we all can’t breathe. People can’t understand a simple message because they think every statement is about religion. It’s not. It’s about AIR. And children are struggling. So to make it simple for you – it is the irresponsible actions of people that seem to be anti national. To me. And should also be to you. Because it’s your children, everyone’s children irrespective of which religion they belong to., that are suffering. And so are the citizens of this country. I’m assuming that also includes you.
— Soni Razdan (@Soni_Razdan) November 5, 2026

An Estonian newspaper recently revealed that a British soldier disobeyed a direct order to remove the SIM card from his cellphone before being deployed to a part of Estonia, approximately 90 miles west of the Russian border.
As a result of his refusal to engage in this element of operational security (opsec), the soldier, Daniel Barton-Kennedy, had his phone hacked, and nude photos of himself were stolen and used as blackmail against him.
Eventually, Barton-Kennedy was court-martialed for disobeying a lawful command, pled guilty, was reduced in rank, and ordered to serve 10 months in detention.
According to a 21-page British appeals court document shared with Ars Technica by Eesti Ekspress, the Estonian newspaper that first reported on this saga, the story begins in January 2026.
At the time, Barton-Kennedy was a corporal, with over seven years of service, serving in the 1st Battalion of the Duke of Lancaster Regiment of the British Army.
His unit was deployed to participate in “Exercise Eastern Warrior” in Tapa, Estonia, roughly halfway between Tallinn, the capital city, and the Estonia-Russia border.
While in the United Kingdom, on January 7, Barton-Kennedy, along with other members of his unit, were briefed on their orders and given specific instructions to “remove SIM cards and switch off location settings and to use a trusted virtual private network on all personal electronic devices.”
Once the unit arrived in Estonia, days later, they were given further briefings and reminders of this policy. Despite this, Barton-Kennedy ignored the instruction.

Delhi’s pollution woes worsen ahead of Diwali firecrackers, air quality ‘very poor’
Of the 59 monitoring stations that recorded data on Sunday, air quality was in the 'severe' category at 12 and in the 'very poor' category at 22.
Delhi's air quality was in the 'very poor' category on Sunday, but set to worsen after Diwali celebrations in the evening.
The average Air Quality Index (AQI) for the day settled at 376 in the 'very poor' category as a thick layer of smog enveloped the city and reduced visibility.
The air quality is forecast to turn 'severe' on Monday following Diwali celebrations, combined with vehicular emissions, as well as the peak stubble-burning season.
Also read: Delhi breathes worst air on Diwali eve in 10 years
Deep Dive
Of the 59 monitoring stations that recorded data on Sunday, air quality was in the 'severe' category at 12 and in the 'very poor' category at 22. The worst AQI was recorded in Jahangirpuri at 463.
The city's average AQI increased from 369 on Saturday to 376 on Sunday, remaining not far from the 'severe' threshold of 400. Several monitoring stations have already breached this mark, indicating deterioration in air quality across the capital.
According to the Air Quality Early Warning System (EWS) for Delhi, the air quality is likely to remain in the 'severe' category from November 9 for a few days.
As per the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), an AQI between 0 and 50 is classified as 'good', 51 and 100 as 'satisfactory', 101 and 200 as 'moderate', 201 and 300 as 'poor', 301 and 400 as 'very poor', and 401 and 500 as 'severe'.
Also read: Diwali eve crackers leave Delhi under a toxic haze, air quality nears ‘severe’
Weather and air quality experts have attributed the anticipated deterioration to unfavourable meteorological conditions, the onset of Diwali-related celebrations and vehicular emissions, along with the peak period of stubble burning in neighbouring states.
Unfavourable meteorological conditions are further aggravating the situation. According to the EWS, a ventilation index below 6,000 square metres per second, coupled with an average wind speed of less than 10 kilometres per hour, is unfavourable for the effective dispersion of pollutants.
PM2.5 was the predominant pollutant in the national capital on Sunday, with emissions from firecrackers adding to the levels of particulate matter.
According to the Decision Support System (DSS) for Delhi, the transport sector is set to be the largest contributor to the city's pollution on Sunday, accounting for 19 per cent.
Stubble burning is set to contribute 3.5 per cent, with forecasts suggesting that the contribution might remain around 2.99 per cent on Monday.

Turkey's President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Azerbaijan's President Ilham Aliyev vowed on Sunday (November 8, 2026) that their countries' alliance would remain solid, in a show of unity aimed at overcoming a public rift between the close neighbours.
Tensions flared in September, when Baku revised school uniform regulations to prohibit clothing deemed incompatible with secular education, effectively barring Islamic headscarves in classrooms.
Mr. Erdogan's government has dismantled restrictions on hijabs in Turkey.
Azerbaijan's move sparked protests at home and drew criticism from Mr. Erdogan's Islamist-rooted Justice and Development Party (AKP). Presidential adviser Oktay Saral demanded that Azerbaijan reverse the restrictions.
Mr. Aliyev's ruling party, Yeni Azerbaijan, denounced the comments as "interference in Azerbaijan's internal affairs".
Baku also declared 31 Turkish nationals, including an Opposition lawmaker and party leaders, persona non grata over critical social media posts.
Mr. Erdogan subsequently dismissed Mr. Saral, but Mr. Aliyev stayed away from an October 30 summit of Turkic leaders in Ankara — despite a personal invitation from Mr. Erdogan. Instead, he sent Foreign Minister Jeyhun Bayramov.
On Sunday (November 8, 2026), as Azerbaijan marked Victory Day commemorating a 2020 war with Armenia, Mr. Erdogan arrived in the country's Fuzuli district, which Baku recaptured from Armenian forces six years ago.
A guard of honour lined up at the airport, where Mr. Aliyev and First Lady Mehriban Aliyeva, welcomed Mr. Erdogan and his wife Ms. Emine.
"With the permission of Almighty God, our unity will endure forever," Mr. Erdogan told a joint press conference with Mr. Aliyev.
"This unity of hearts, which we describe with the motto 'One Nation, Two States,' is an everlasting torch that draws strength from our shared past and illuminates our future."
Mr. Aliyev said the alliance — "an important factor across a vast geographical area" — remained unshaken.
"Together, Azerbaijan and Turkey are even stronger," he said, adding that Mr. Erdogan's visit "shows the whole world our unity".
"I am confident that this unity will last forever."
'Deeper rift'
Analysts say the quarrel reflects deeper unease over Baku's diplomatic independence and its close ties to Israel.
"Azerbaijan-Turkey tensions stemmed from the fact that Baku does not see itself as the younger brother in this alliance and insists on relations between equal partners," Elkhan Shahinoglu, head of the Baku-based Atlas Research Centre, told AFP.
"The hijab dispute is a symptom of a deeper rift," Gonul Tol, an analyst at the Washington-based Middle East Institute, wrote on X.
"Tensions have long simmered over a number of issues including Azerbaijan's sovereignty, Ankara's influence in Baku, diverging policies toward Israel, and Turkey's rapprochement with Armenia."
Baku has forged strong military and economic ties with Israel, which supplied Azerbaijan with weapons during its 2020 war with Armenia over the breakaway Karabakh region.
This angered Turkey, which has grown increasingly hostile towards Israel over the Gaza war. Mr. Erdogan has accused Israel of "genocide".
Turkey is also seeking to normalise relations with Armenia, whose border it closed in the 1990s in solidarity with Azerbaijan, while linking progress to Armenian-Azerbaijani peace efforts.
November 8 marks Azerbaijan's capture of the city of Shusha in Karabakh during its war with Armenia, a victory achieved with Turkish backing.
The Turkic-speaking allies describe their relationship as "one nation, two states" and, despite the friction, remain closely bound by military and energy ties.
Turkey serves as a key transit route for Azerbaijani oil and gas exports to Western markets.
An ex-Soviet republic, Azerbaijan is a mainly Shiite Muslim country, but after decades of Soviet rule it emerged as one of the most secular states in the Muslim world.

Rosemary Nyirumbe became a nun when she was just in her mid-teens – and she felt her true vocation lay in rehabilitating children who had been through some of the worst trauma imaginable. So that’s what she did. In this episode Mike Wooldridge hears Sr Rosemary’s astonishing story. The feared rebel group, the Lord’s Resistance Army, started to terrorise the north of Uganda in the 1980s. Many children, girls as well as boys, were abducted and forced to become child soldiers. In many cases, the LRA forced them to commit atrocities, leaving them deeply traumatised. Many of the girls also bore the children of rebel leaders. As they started to return home, these children were often rejected by their families and communities, says Sr Rosemary. So she set about giving them a future and a hope: through enabling them to acquire skills like sewing, and by helping them see that God had not rejected them for the atrocities they had been forced to commit. More than once, Sr Rosemary put herself in enormous danger in order to fulfil her mission. But, she says, she also learnt that small acts of kindness can touch the hearts of even battle-hardened rebels.

How infant deaths in Keralam’s Attappady expose a deep-rooted health, social crisis
12 infants, including 10 tribals, have died in Attappady this year, sparking a political row as the State government orders an expert probe. Tribal activists say the crisis demands action beyond healthcare, addressing malnutrition, anaemia and deep-rooted social issues
Published - October 31, 2026 01:25 pm IST - PALAKKAD
In Attappady, maternal health remains a major concern. Anaemia among pregnant women continues to be widespread, while underweight mothers and low birth weight among newborns add to the risks (file image)
| Photo Credit: The Hindu
The deaths of 12 infants, 10 of them from tribal communities, in Attappady in Keralam in recent months have once again cast a spotlight on a child health crisis that has defied solutions for over a decade. While the State government has set an expert assessment in motion, tribal organisations maintain that the roots of the crisis run deeper than healthcare, demanding sustained action on nutrition, maternal health, landlessness and the wider socio-economic conditions of the community.
Figures cited by tribal activists show that 124 infants have died in the region since 2011. Since 2012, Attappady has also recorded around 300 abortions, 90 intrauterine deaths and two dozen stillbirths. The region came under particular scrutiny in 2013, when 47 tribal infants died. Tribal observers estimate that around 10 children have died annually over the years.

Saudi airstrikes on homes near Yemen’s capital kill 33 people
Sanaa says many people are still buried under rubble

At least 33 people were killed and 39 wounded after Saudi Arabia conducted airstrikes on a town near the Yemeni capital of Sanaa on Saturday, the Saba news agency reported.
This is one of the deadliest attacks in Yemen since the Saudis renewed their war against Ansarullah, the coalition that governs most of the impoverished Arab nation and is commonly known as the Houthis, in July.
Saudi Arabia's Centre for International Communication said it was “investigating the report”.
The renewed fighting has shattered a 2022 truce brokered by the UN. Saudi Arabia has carried out airstrikes across Yemen and backed its local allies to launch offensives against Ansarullah positions. Ansarullah, in turn, have launched missile and drone attacks on Saudi military facilities, airports and oil infrastructure. They have also carried out lightning counteroffensives against Saudi-backed forces on the ground, capturing vast swathes of territory in the process and tightening their control over Bab el Mandeb, a critical maritime chokepoint in the Red Sea. Ansarullah are currently fighting Saudi-backed forces for control of the strategic city of Taiz.
The airstrikes on Sunday hit homes in the town of Bani Hushaish and killed mostly women and children, the health ministry in Sanaa said.
Anees Alasbahi, a spokesperson for the ministry, told Al-Masirah TV that many people were still buried under the rubble as subsequent strikes targeted emergency workers trying to pull out survivors.
Footage broadcast by Al-Masirah TV of the aftermath of the strikes showed staff carrying limp bodies of multiple young children out of ambulances at a local hospital. One little girl's head had been cleaved open. Other children lay on stretchers, bloodied and bandaged as staff tended to them. A wounded man covered in dust was still wearing a first responder's orange vest as he was helped out of an ambulance.
“The strikes keep coming. Just as rescuers arrive, another strike hits. We have even lost some of our own medical responders who have been martyred," Abdul-Aziz al-Dailami, the director of Sehatuna Hospital in Sanaa, told Reuters. "We received a number of wounded people in very critical condition, with injuries to the head, chest and legs as well as fractures.”
The ongoing fighting has revived a 12-year war in Yemen that has caused one of the worst humanitarian crises globally and fragmented the Arab world's most impoverished country.
The war has killed at least 150,000 people, according to the UN, and caused widespread deaths from hunger and disease outbreaks.
The number of people displaced since the latest round of fighting began has climbed to over 200,000, the International Organization for Migration said in October.

An infant in Wisconsin has died of measles, the first measles death in the state since 1990, officials reported Thursday. The death comes amid an outbreak in the Badger State that has stricken over 430 people across 13 counties this year.
“Any death of a child is a tragedy, and even more so when it is related to a vaccine-preventable disease,” Wisconsin Health Secretary Kirsten Johnson said in a statement. “Measles can cause serious illness and death, and it is important for all Wisconsinites to evaluate their risk and take steps to protect themselves and their family.”
The baby’s death is the third measles fatality nationally just this week, following the death of a New York child reported on Monday and another death in Pennsylvania reported on Wednesday. The Pennsylvania death was of an unvaccinated person in Jefferson County; the state health department did not provide additional details, such as the age of the person. The state’s explosive, ongoing measles outbreak has led to 1,467 cases so far this year.
In all, there have been nine reported measles deaths this year in the US, eight of which have been confirmed by state officials. The deaths include the baby’s death in Wisconsin, the child’s death in New York, and seven deaths (six confirmed) in Pennsylvania, including two babies, a healthy teen, and several adults with underlying health conditions.
National context
As of November 5, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention is reporting 5,182 measles cases in the US this year across 47 states and jurisdictions. The CDC is reporting four measles deaths, though it’s unclear which of the reported deaths the CDC has counted.
The national case and death tallies are the highest recorded since 1991, though the reported cases likely represent a significant undercount of actual cases. As Wisconsin health officials noted in the announcement of the baby’s death, “Not everyone who becomes ill seeks medical care or gets tested, which means cases may go unreported.” This is particularly true given that large outbreaks, including the one ongoing in Pennsylvania, have struck in tight-knit religious communities that are less likely to seek conventional medical care.

What new Kane deal means for England and the Premier League record
- Published
Harry Kane's decision to sign a new contract with Bayern Munich carries heavy significance for the Bundesliga giants, who have been celebrating his status as a Ballon d'Or winner, but also for England and the Premier League's record books.
Bayern have acted swiftly to secure the 33-year-old on a deal taking him through to 2029 after he was crowned the world's best player, ensuring England's captain and record goalscorer will spend the final peak years of a magnificent career at Allianz Arena.
Kane has written himself into Bayern legend since joining from Spurs for £86m in August 2023, scoring 102 goals in 102 Bundesliga matches, winning two league titles and three successive Golden Boot awards.
It is why Bayern could not contemplate his departure as other clubs eyed his next move - and why the announcement Kane is staying casts ripples far beyond Munich.
Does it mean Kane will never grace the Premier League again? And does it mean - far more enticingly - he has his sights set on two more major tournaments and two more chances to grasp the prize that has eluded him at international level?
Former England striker Chris Sutton told BBC Sport: "I certainly think, although you always have to factor fitness issues into all of this, that Harry is more than capable of carrying on for a few years yet, easily.
"People might say his game lacks a little bit of pace, but he's so strong in other areas. He is a world-class all-round player. His finishing isn't going to be affected in any way by his age. He can still link up play and his football brain is first class.
"I don't see his age being such a big deal. You think of pacy players over the years who rely on that part of the game then lose it as they get older. Harry is not one of those. He seems fit and at the peak of his powers with Bayern and England."
Kane's new contract expires shortly before his 36th birthday, certainly raising the prospect the player who left Spurs as the highest scorer in their history with 280 goals in 435 appearances may never grace the Premier League again.
His consummate professionalism, and apparent ability to develop into the complete player with age, means this can never be discounted.
The notion of an emotional return to Spurs at some point has often provided background noise, but now looks increasingly unlikely.
What it surely means is that Alan Shearer will remain the Premier League's highest scorer - who knows what will happen with Erling Haaland as Manchester City await punishment after being found guilty of breaching financial regulations they deny? - and out of Kane's reach.
Shearer scored 260 goals in 441 Premier League matches for Blackburn Rovers and Newcastle United. Kane scored 213 times in 320 league games for Spurs.
With Kane still 47 short of Shearer's record, it would need a spectacular late-career flourish for him to eclipse the Geordie icon's tally to write another entry into the history books, which also have him as England's highest scorer with 91 goals from a record-equalling 125 caps.
What will be of huge interest to Thomas Tuchel - the coach who took him to Bayern and now leads England - is that Kane has delivered a clear indication that Euro 2028, to be played in the UK and Ireland, is firmly in his sights.
And, when this new deal expires, Kane is also only a year away from the 2030 World Cup, to be played in Morocco, Portugal and Spain, with special centenary opening matches held in Uruguay, Argentina, and Paraguay.
This, of course, is a stretch given the inevitable rigours of age, but few who know Kane, who have watched him move to a new level at Bayern, would ever say never to such a driven personality, hiding fierce mental strength and a competitive instinct behind his humble 'anti-superstar' persona.
Sutton said: "Euro 2028 certainly shouldn't be a problem and who knows beyond that? If Harry has got players around him with pace and dynamism, as well as runners in and around him, then his football brain isn't going to change and he can still play a huge part.
"He's such a sharp, quick, thinker. He reads the game superbly, knows where his next pass is going and has shown an ability to drop deep and impact the game.
"Harry just seems to be getting better and more rounded with age. And as for age, just look at someone like Teddy Sheringham. He was playing and scoring goals for West Ham United in the Premier League in his 40s.
"Sheringham was an incredibly talented player with supreme intelligence. Harry Kane falls right into the same category.
"Ronaldo has just retired from international football with Portugal at 41, but he is a totally different player than Harry Kane. Harry is one who can drop a little bit deeper to use his incredible ability and range of passing.
"As well as that ability, it is about how Harry's football brain works as much as anything and that won't change with age."
And it is an argument, and a hope, that is even more pertinent as England still do not possess any other striker or forward who could be considered anywhere near Kane's class or potency.
"When you talk about 2028 or 2030, who are the English strikers coming through to challenge him to take him out of the team?" said Sutton. "There's no-one in his class or effectiveness, or anywhere near it."
What also plays into the argument that Kane cannot be ruled out of such long-term involvement is the manner in which he responded so superbly to what was a disappointing Euro 2024, not only as England lost in the final to Spain but because he looked a jaded shadow of his old self.
Kane looked so out of sorts there was a clamour for him to be replaced by Ollie Watkins, then at Aston Villa. He was substituted in all of England's knockout matches, including after only 61 minutes of that final loss to Spain in Berlin.
And yet, Kane still finished as the tournament's joint top scorer with three goals from seven games.
The notion of him being replaced with the stakes so high now is unthinkable, such is his peerless form and stature.
While Bayern are convinced their new investment in Kane's brilliance will be rewarded with further honours, Tuchel will hope it is motivation and inspiration to finally end the country's long wait for international glory.
